stronger_left_out.name: Wittenoom
stronger_left_out.reason: Unsafe and closed (brief rule): an asbestos-contaminated ghost town the state has closed and degazetted; Wikivoyage says photograph the 'Keep out' signs and move on.

stronger_left_out.name: Montebello Islands
stronger_left_out.reason: Held for the owner (review): Wikivoyage: 'beyond a day trip', 'boat tours sometimes visit'; reached only by liveaboard charter, so few visitors can go. Case for: two counted sources and a distinctive history.

stronger_left_out.name: Barrow Island
stronger_left_out.reason: Rule 2: only company-authorised visitors may land (Wikivoyage Onslow and Pilbara: 'no public access').

stronger_left_out.name: Juukan Gorge
stronger_left_out.reason: Rule 2: no public access or visitor facilities; the rock shelters were destroyed in 2020 and the gorge sits on a mining lease. Wikivoyage mentions it only as history.

stronger_left_out.name: Mount Meharry
stronger_left_out.reason: Held for the owner (review): No counted visitor source names it as somewhere to go (hiking guide and 4WD forums only); remote, unsigned access through mining country. Case for: a 'highest point in the state' summit with a monument that 4WD travellers do seek out.

stronger_left_out.name: Jigalong
stronger_left_out.reason: Rule 2: an Aboriginal community, not a visitor attraction; entry to WA Aboriginal communities needs permission and Wikivoyage names nothing to see or do there (only its rabbit-proof-fence history).

stronger_left_out.name: Burrup Peninsula
stronger_left_out.reason: Duplicate of Murujuga National Park: ANW titles the park 'Murujuga National Park (Burrup Peninsula)'; the peninsula's visitor draws are the park's petroglyphs (Ngajarli) and Hearson's Cove, the rest is industrial port land.

stronger_left_out.name: Mount Whaleback
stronger_left_out.reason: Held for the owner (review): The mine is a company site seen only on a booked tour on select dates; COVERAGE says the place a tour goes is the spot, but here the place is closed to anyone off the tour.

stronger_left_out.name: Depuch Island
stronger_left_out.reason: No counted source found; an offshore island with rock art reached only by private boat (rule 1).

stronger_left_out.name: Nanny Goat Hill
stronger_left_out.reason: No counted source (Wikipedia only) and part of Cossack; its candidate coordinates (45.41, -75.71) are in Ottawa, Canada, so the record is also wrong.

stronger_left_out.name: Direction Island
stronger_left_out.reason: Duplicate/part of the Mackerel Islands group already covered by Thevenard Island; a cabin island whose draw is the same reef fishing and snorkelling, and Wikivoyage reports it closed with no ferry (2022).

stronger_left_out.name: Mikurrunya Hills
stronger_left_out.reason: Held for the owner (review): One source; a roadside look 50 km from town.

stronger_left_out.name: Handrail Pool
stronger_left_out.reason: Part of a larger spot: the Handrail Pool trail is the walk down Weano Gorge (DBCA: 'the 1.5km return Handrail Pool trail in Weano Gorge'); keep it inside the Weano Gorge spot's bio.

stronger_left_out.name: Oxers Lookout
stronger_left_out.reason: Held for the owner (review): It sits at the end of Weano Road in the same day-use area as Weano Gorge and Handrail Pool (within ~1 km); a separate spot may duplicate Weano Gorge. Case for: a distinct viewpoint over four gorges that many treat as Karijini's top view.

stronger_left_out.name: Fortescue Falls
stronger_left_out.reason: Held for the owner (review): It lies inside Dales Gorge (about 1 km from the recreation area); listing both may be a near-duplicate. Owner to choose: Dales Gorge as the spot with the falls in its bio, or the falls as the spot.

stronger_left_out.name: Mackerel Islands
stronger_left_out.reason: Duplicate of Thevenard Island: the 'Mackerel Islands' is an unofficial group name (Wikivoyage) whose visitor island is Thevenard; keep one spot, under the name the proposer prefers.

stronger_left_out.name: Fern Pool
stronger_left_out.reason: Part of a larger spot: Fern Pool is in Dales Gorge a few hundred metres from Fortescue Falls (Wikivoyage lists them as one entry 'Fortescue Falls and Fern Pool (in Dales Gorge)').

stronger_left_out.name: Circular Pool Lookout
stronger_left_out.reason: Part of a larger spot: a rim lookout at the start of the Gorge Rim Walk over Dales Gorge (rule 3, an outlook on a track).

stronger_left_out.name: Gorge Rim Walk
stronger_left_out.reason: Part of a larger spot: a 2.4 km rim walk along Dales Gorge linking two of its lookouts; belongs in the Dales Gorge spot (rule 3).

stronger_left_out.name: Cliff Lookout
stronger_left_out.reason: Held for the owner (review): One source and a short look from a car park inside Millstream; may be one of the lookouts on Snappy Gum Drive and so part of a larger spot.

stronger_left_out.name: Mount Herbert
stronger_left_out.reason: Held for the owner (review): One source; a short walk near Python Pool, likely folded into Python Pool or the Camel Trail.

stronger_left_out.name: Snappy Gum Drive
stronger_left_out.reason: Held for the owner (review): A drive (a route on the way between the park's spots) rather than a place; one source; arguably part of the park spot.

stronger_left_out.name: North West Shelf Visitor Centre
stronger_left_out.reason: Rule 4/2: Wikivoyage gives it about three hours a week (usually Wednesday mornings), an industrial company information centre; not there when a visitor arrives.

stronger_left_out.name: Vodka Beach
stronger_left_out.reason: Part of a larger spot: a camping beach on Trimouille Island within the Montebello Islands (rule 3).

stronger_left_out.name: Onslow Point Lookout
stronger_left_out.reason: Held for the owner (review): One source, a short look in town; part of the Onslow town spot (its beaches and walkway).

stronger_left_out.name: Wheatstone
stronger_left_out.reason: Not a place a visitor can go: a Chevron gas plant seen only on a monthly May-Oct tour (an occasion, rule 4; a company site, rule 2).

stronger_left_out.name: Six Mile Creek
stronger_left_out.reason: Held for the owner (review): One source, no coordinates; reads as a locals' fishing spot at the edge of town (COVERAGE: places only locals use fail).

stronger_left_out.name: Redbank Bridge Lookout
stronger_left_out.reason: Held for the owner (review): One source; a roadside pull-out with a ten-minute look.

stronger_left_out.name: Cossack Museum
stronger_left_out.reason: Part of a larger spot: the museum in the old courthouse is inside the Cossack ghost town (ANW: 'the Courthouse, now the Cossack Museum' on the Cossack Heritage Trail); belongs in Cossack's bio.

stronger_left_out.name: Jarman Island
stronger_left_out.reason: Held for the owner (review): One source, and it names it as a view from Cossack rather than a place to go; only by boat.

stronger_left_out.name: Tien Tsin Lookout
stronger_left_out.reason: Part of a larger spot: ANW names Tien Tsin lookout as a stop on the Cossack Heritage Trail; belongs in Cossack's bio (rule 3).

stronger_left_out.name: Reader Head Lookout
stronger_left_out.reason: Re-looked for a counted source and found none (Wikipedia mention only); a roadside lookout between Cossack and Point Samson (rule 1, rule 3).

stronger_left_out.name: Chinaman's Pool
stronger_left_out.reason: Held for the owner (review): Near-duplicate: it is 'just beside Marble Bar Pool' (the jasper bar the town is named for), so the two are one swimming stop; keep the Marble Bar Pool spot if that is listed.

stronger_left_out.name: North Pole
stronger_left_out.reason: No counted source; a remote geological site (stromatolites) with no visitor facilities (rule 1, rule 2).

stronger_left_out_note: The lowest kept score is 0 views (Mount Nameless, 0 counted sources by the script's count but re-looked to one), so every reject and review is at least level with it and all 34 are listed, strongest first, each with its What-qualifies reason. Highest left out: Wittenoom (124,640 views, closed and unsafe), Montebello Islands (23,611, review), Barrow Island (21,805, no public access), Juukan Gorge (13,985, no access).
benchmark: Not applicable: the COVERAGE.md benchmark places are New Zealand. Pilbara analogues applied: a gateway village whose draw is the journey beyond it is not kept outright (Tom Price and Paraburdoo are kept as towns but placed standalone, not as destinations); a vehicle or tour is never the spot (Dampier Archipelago, not a cruise; Thevenard Island, not the ferry; Mount Whaleback mine tour held in review); a recurring phenomenon becomes its place (Staircase to the Moon -> Cooke Point); a long feature is placed where visitors reach it (Hamersley Gorge inside Karijini, Python Pool and Deep Reach Pool at their own points).
